reasons.plausibility: The proposed mechanism that controlled annealing can partially disrupt lamellar boundary coherency to reduce dislocation pile-ups and thus improve ductility while retaining strength is well-grounded in solid materials science principles, with only minor uncertainties about the precise annealing conditions.
reasons.testability: The hypothesis outlines a direct and clear experimental comparison between annealed and unannealed samples with measurable indicators (dislocation pile-ups, microcrack formation, mechanical properties), providing a robust path to falsification.
reasons.usefulness: Focusing on an accessible thermal treatment to address the known brittleness of eutectic high-entropy alloys makes this hypothesis highly relevant and of practical use to researchers aiming to enhance ductility without compromising strength.
